issue.title: Hydrate the RN web drawing screen in tiers so drawing goes live first
issue.body:
## What

Make the React Native web export's drawing screen go live in tiers instead of all at once, in the owner's order:

0. everything visible;
1. the drawing engine, as soon as possible;
2. palette, brushes, stroke width and Undo;
3. Clear, drawer, coloring book and AI;
4. the settings cog and parent gate, last.

Today one whole-tree hydration makes every tier live together.

## Why

The prerendered first frame (#3006, ADR-0180) paints at 724 ms on a throttled phone, but the drawing engine listens only at about 2,642 ms and the controls at 2,519 ms. Until then the shell answers touches with a burst and a "not yet" wiggle. Tiering would let a child draw sooner.

## How much it can buy (measured for ADR-0180)

The entry chunk's source map (`docs/scratchpad/2026-10-19-rn-web-static-first-paint/results/early-input/entry-attribution.json`) bounds it:

| Part | Bytes |
| --- | ---: |
| Libraries that must load before anything hydrates (React DOM, React Native Web, React, Expo runtime, others) | about 390,000 |
| Drawing engine | 100,093 |
| Drawing chrome (palette, actions panel, Clear, drawer) | 122,111 |
| Product, settings and the library | 75,576 |
| Platform seams | 27,517 |
| Other app code | 25,029 |

- **What tier 1 needs.** A tier-1 chunk needs the libraries, the engine and most of the seams: about 70% of the entry's bytes.
- **The gain.** At Slow 4G throughput that brings the engine forward by about 0.3 s, not to first paint.
- **The floor.** The libraries alone take about 0.5 s to arrive.

## Where

- **Hydration split.** Suspense boundaries with lazy chunks around each tier, in `experiments/native-architecture/src/` (the drawing screen's tree).
- **Per-tier release.** Per-tier stamps like `data-controls-live` (`src/platform/firstFrameControls.web.ts`, `src/platform/firstFrameContract.ts`). The boot script's guard in `tools/migration/prerender-native-web.mjs` can then release each tier as it goes live. React event replay is not needed and was never verified with React Native Web's pressables.
- **Startup caps.** `tools/migration/check-native-web-startup.mjs` holds the first-paint and core-controls caps (ADR-0179, ADR-0180). A tier split changes what each cap counts.

## Done when

- **Earlier drawing.** On the ADR-0180 phone measurement (devtools throttling, first visit, quiet host, median of three), a finger on the paper becomes ink measurably earlier than 2,642 ms. Each tier's live time is recorded.
- **Nothing regresses.** First paint, LCP and the pixel identity of the prerendered frame are unchanged. Both startup caps pass.
- **The design is recorded.** An ADR amending ADR-0180 records the built design, written with the implementation.

Not started: the owner deferred it on 2026-10-19 ("Tiers issue, keep Node"), when ADR-0180 became Active for what is built.

Refs #2690
